title: Strategic plan 2024-2027 and permanent patio program
subtitle: Also: by-law review work plan, noise cameras, backyard fires, fireworks, e-scooters and paramedic response times.
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended that Council approve Future Guelph, the city's strategic plan for 2024-2027 {{vote:m1}}. Costs will be dealt with in the multi-year budget process, and staff will report on performance indicators in the fall. It also recommended making the seasonal patio program permanent, subject to budget approval {{vote:m5}}. Proposals to phase in the higher patio fees and to study downtown parking relief were withdrawn. Staff will provide more information, including on funding the program with the municipal accommodation tax, before Council meets at the end of the month.

On the by-law work plan, the committee asked staff to report back by October on what could be removed to make room for reviews of noise rules (including vehicle noise cameras), outdoor recreational fires and fireworks. Several of these motions were reworded so they ask staff to explore options rather than set the outcome. The committee also recommended allowing personal e-scooters from August 1, 2023 {{vote:m21}}.
The committee also accepted the 2024 paramedic response time plan {{vote:m6}}. Final decisions on all recommendations rest with Council.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the plan, referring its costs to the multi-year budget process and directing staff to share final key performance indicators in an information report in fall 2023.
The committee recommended approving the seasonal patio program as described in the staff report, pending budget approval in the 2024-2027 multi-year budget.
The committee recommended setting the 2024 response time performance plan as staff recommended and receiving the 2022 response time report for information.

decisions.item: By-law reviews to drop from work plan
decisions.detail: Staff are to report back by October 2023 on any by-law reviews that could be removed from the work plan to free up resources.

decisions.item: Noise by-law and vehicle noise cameras
decisions.detail: Staff are to report by October 2023 on timelines to update the noise by-law, including exploring vehicle noise cameras and other noise issues.
Staff are to report by October 2023 on timelines to review the outdoor recreational fire by-law, including possible use of smokeless recreational wood-burning fires.
Staff are to report by October 2023 on timelines for a full engagement process on the deployment, use and sale of fireworks in Guelph.
The committee recommended that Council approve the draft by-law and Traffic By-law amendments to permit personal e-scooters effective August 1, 2023.

debate: On the strategic plan, trail group delegates urged that closing the missing Guelph section of the regional rail trail be funded in the multi-year budget, citing tourism and economic benefits. One councillor questioned whether it ranked as a priority for neighbourhoods lacking basic connections. The mayor said project-level funding belongs in budget discussions, not the plan.

Councillors also asked staff about accessibility compliance by 2025 and about keeping affordability visible. Staff said a tax burden measure will remain among the performance indicators and the city will meet accessibility requirements.

Patio delegates backed the program but warned that the much higher on-street fees could push out smaller operators. Councillors questioned using the municipal accommodation tax to cover part of the cost, with one opposed and others citing loss of public space. Staff said the funding split fits the user fee policy and agreed to provide more information, including legal advice.

On the by-law motions, some councillors said the original wording pre-judged outcomes and that staff capacity is limited. The CEO said each item would displace other work and some options, such as noise cameras or backyard fires, might prove unworkable. Wording was changed to explore. A delegate supported noise cameras, citing health effects of vehicle noise.

On fireworks, supporters cited effects on pets and people with trauma, and air pollution. Others questioned whether a ban could be enforced or would only move purchases to nearby cities. On e-scooters, a delegate asked that multi-use paths be allowed. An amendment was withdrawn after staff said they would first review safety and liability.
